executive_assessment.text: Named Papua weather-displacement cases and Nusa Tenggara livelihood/water concerns add subnational context; existing conflict and climate pressure are not merged into an unsupported causal claim.

East Kalimantan and South Sumatra face prospective coal-transition distributional risks. Local governance and village finance offer capacities, with reported outputs and intentions kept separate from evaluated results.

geographic_notes.text: Source dated 2023-11 reports: The study places weather-related displacement among the human-security concerns of conflict-afflicted Papuans: extreme rain and flash floods near the Cyclops Mountains killed at least 50 people and displaced thousands in 2019; prolonged drought and extreme cold displaced 6,000 people from Agandugume and Lambewi in 2023.

Source dated 2023-11-27 reports: The World Bank identifies East Kalimantan and South Sumatra as coal-dependent regions where a transition could bring job losses, worker-family dislocation, inequality, and reduced service access; without mitigation, these effects could heighten mistrust, insecurity, and social instability.
Source dated 2023-11-27 reports: The report identifies local knowledge and governance as resilience assets, but says village budgets are not yet optimized for climate-smart development.

Source dated 2025-10-17 reports: The UNDP-led mixed-method study focuses on West and East Nusa Tenggara and identifies climate change as a direct threat to local livelihoods, water resources, food security, and community resilience.
Source dated 2025-10-17 reports: The publisher says local knowledge can help mitigate and resolve human conflicts that may emerge from climate impacts in the two Nusa Tenggara provinces.

Source dated 2026-04-27 reports: A World Bank brief describes restored West Java slopes and springs managed through a village-owned water enterprise; in Margagiri, village micro-dams, drainage, and agroforestry reportedly reduced heavy-rain damage and improved farm output.

known_gaps.text: Automated machine-screening is not independent source verification. Routine/default app-use approval does not certify claims or sources. 8 of 8 evidence records and 1 of 1 pathways lack claim-level verification in this remediation; review the linked records before relying on them.
The directly reviewed sources do not establish that conflict changes climate exposure or blocks climate-adaptation access in Indonesia; this reverse link remains unverified.
RSIS reports weather displacement affecting conflict-afflicted Papua, while explicitly distinguishing those events from the causes of internal conflict.
The UNDP 2025 report PDF could not be directly inspected because of its browser extraction size limit; its claims use only the opened official publisher summary and are not village-specific.
The directly opened World Bank Social Dimensions file is an executive-summary extract; detailed district findings in the full report were not used.
Papua hazard displacement is retained as differentiated vulnerability, not climate causation of armed conflict or a verified reverse insecurity mechanism.
The coal-transition pathway concerns prospective distributional risks from mitigation policy, not physical hazard attribution; no observed local instability or conflict reduction is inferred.
The Nusa Tenggara publisher synopsis cannot support village-specific conflict cases or independently evaluated mediation outcomes.
Routine/default app-use approval granted by Lindsey Jones on 2026-10-27; independent source verification remains incomplete. Lending eligibility is not an FCV classification.
